events.summary: The Financial Times reported that OpenAI's annualized revenue was about $50 billion at end-September, $20 billion below the widely reported figure; AI-related stocks fell (Nasdaq -1.3%, S&P 500 -0.5%; Marvell, Arm and Intel down more than 6%, Micron over 5%). The Motley Fool also cited news that an Nvidia-backed Australian data-center firm had not attracted the hoped-for support, 'raising questions about AI funding'. Bond yields were near 5.2-5.3% and oil jumped. Data-center builders fell together (equal-weight mean of 8 peers -1.60%); Sterling fell 2.94%.
events.why_it_matters: Sterling's growth is mostly data-center site work; investors sell it when they doubt that the money for AI data centers (ultimately paid for by AI revenue) will keep flowing. No company or customer cut its plans; this was a sentiment move. On Friday Bloomberg reported OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70 billion annualized revenue by year end (per Yahoo live blog), which partly answered the worry.

products.name: E-Infrastructure Solutions (site development plus CEC mission-critical electrical)
products.what_it_is: Preparing huge plots of land for data centers, chip plants and big factories: clearing, levelling, foundations, underground utilities; since the CEC acquisition also electrical work inside those sites.
products.analogy: The crew that levels the lot and digs the foundation before a house goes up, but for buildings the size of several football fields.
products.buyers: Data-center owners (hyperscalers and developers), semiconductor and manufacturing companies, large warehouse developers. Customer names not disclosed.
products.how_it_works: Paid per project under contracts; signed contracts sit in backlog until the work is done. Data-center campuses often come in phases, so one customer can award follow-on 'future phase' work.
products.sales: Segment revenue $905.0m in Q2 2026, +192% year on year (as cited in the 2026-10-07 report from the Q2 release). E-Infrastructure signed backlog +165% year on year; mission-critical projects were 92% of E-Infrastructure backlog at 2026-06-30. Company backlog $4.33bn (+116%; +50% organic); combined backlog incl. $1.28bn unsigned awards $5.62bn; book-to-burn 1.4x (backlog) and 1.3x (combined), excluding Stone Ridge; future-phase pipeline over $1.4bn.
products.stage: Scaling: record revenue and backlog; legacy site development revenue +111% with operating margins up year on year and quarter on quarter (company statement).
products.size_for_company: About 78% of Q2 revenue ($905.0m of $1.168bn; our calculation, from the 2026-10-07 report).
products.competition: Other data-center builders listed: Comfort Systems (FIX, record backlog $14.1bn), Quanta (PWR, backlog $53bn), EMCOR, MYR Group, Primoris, IES, plus many private regional site contractors (peer backlog figures from Nasdaq/Zacks articles, tier 3).
products.why_investors_care: It is the growth engine; the stock trades on whether data-center building keeps expanding.
products.watch_next: Q3 results (est. 2026-11-02): E-Infrastructure backlog, book-to-burn, margins; hyperscaler capex updates in late October.
